context: Sho-young learns about traditional sushi from Hiroshi-elder.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 翔、本格の寿司、食べてみるか。
lines.en: Sho — want to try some authentic sushi?
lines.style: Unhurried, warm invitation. Gentle opening. The patient tone of someone who has all the time in the world. Slight Kansai lilt. Almost conversational—not performing, just asking.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: うん、初心者やけど、冒険する!
lines.en: Yeah—I'm a beginner, but I'm ready to try!
lines.style: Bright, eager surge of energy. Quick pickup on the question. Small boy's genuine excitement—no pretense, just honest enthusiasm. Slight breathlessness on the commitment.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うまい、本格的な味やで。
lines.en: That's good—real, authentic flavor. You'll see.
lines.style: Quiet pride underneath. Soft delivery, almost to himself. The satisfaction of sharing something genuine. Kansai warmth. Steady eye contact level—not lecturing, just confirming.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 熱いお茶も、いただこう。
lines.en: I'll have some hot tea too, please.
lines.style: Polite but natural—not overly formal. A child paying attention to the whole moment, not just the sushi. Warm and present. Small, genuine respect in the tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、本屋で寿司の図書、読んだ。
lines.en: Years ago I read a book about sushi at a bookstore.
lines.style: Drifting into memory. Slow, reflective pace. Soft voice—not wistful, but tender. Kansai ease. The kind of pause that invites listening, not rushing to fill silence.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Next time—I want to read that book!
lines.style: Bright determination underneath. Eager but not demanding. The small, genuine interest of a child who wants to know the same things the adults around him know. Forward-leaning energy.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.style: Simple, warm promise. No fanfare. Kansai ease settling into resolution. The satisfaction of handing something good to someone who'll appreciate it. Slight smile in the voice.
